evidence.claim: Gordan proved in 1868 that the algebra of covariants of any binary form is finitely generated. This is the classical answer to the existence of finite complete covariant systems for one ground form.

Hilbert's 1886 Math. Ann. paper (four pages, written soon after his 1885 doctorate) asked what conditions a form of degree n = μν must satisfy to be a perfect power. This is an example of covariant systems that characterise special forms.
The Hilbert covariant H_{r,d}(F) vanishes exactly when F is the perfect power of an order-r form. These covariants were little studied afterwards, until modern work.
Hilbert's 1890 paper 'Über die Theorie der algebraischen Formen' contains the basis theorem and the syzygy theorem, which settled the general finiteness questions for invariant systems.
Lindemann suggested that Hilbert work on invariant properties of algebraic forms, which is the setting of this early notebook.
